tweets.text: U.S. national debt has now climbed above 100% of GDP for the first time since World War II. That means the country now owes more than the total value of everything it produces in a year, a level typically seen only in major crises or wartime economies. Economists often point out that what matters isn’t just the number itself, but how fast it’s growing and what it costs to service it… but crossing this threshold is still a major long-term signal for the economy. Source: @barchart / Writer: Lynn
